subject.title: refactor(qqbot): install plugin from Tencent package

question: May OpenClaw transfer QQBot ownership to this exact Tencent package only after credential compatibility, prior GHSA mitigations, and the installed-plugin upgrade path are proven?
rationale: The patch deliberately moves executable channel code and security responsibility outside the repository while narrowing an existing credential contract, so accepting or repairing that boundary requires owner and security intent.

options.title: Preserve contracts, then externalize
options.body: Require the external package and OpenClaw migration path to preserve SecretRefs, prior security mitigations, existing install state, and current documentation before merge.

options.title: Approve a breaking cutover
options.body: Explicitly accept the credential and plugin-identity migration burden, with release-visible warnings and an in-product doctor recovery path.

options.title: Keep QQBot monorepo-owned
options.body: Pause the handoff until the external package can meet the shipped compatibility and security contracts without operator-only migration steps.

recommendation.title: Preserve contracts, then externalize
recommendation.body: Require the external package and OpenClaw migration path to preserve SecretRefs, prior security mitigations, existing install state, and current documentation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp is the documented QQ channel owner and is coordinating both sides of this ownership transition.
